title: Confidentiality of Sensitive Data During Transmission
description: Parent registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted from ExternalEntity EE1 to Process P1 may be intercepted during transmission without proper encryption, leading to potential exposure of sensitive personal information.

title: Data Integrity During Transmission
description: Parent registration data transmitted from ExternalEntity EE1 to Process P1 may be altered or tampered with during transmission, potentially resulting in incorrect or malicious data being processed by the authentication service.

title: Unauthorized Access to Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service P1 may be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially allowing them to intercept, modify, or misuse the parent registration data received from ExternalEntity EE1.

title: Excessive data collection for parent account storage
description: The authentication service may collect and store more personal data than strictly necessary for the parent account storage function, violating the minimality principle. This could include unnecessary metadata or derived information that increases privacy risk.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure to third parties
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls, data sharing agreements, or third-party service integrations without explicit consent.

title: Data integrity risk in MongoDB users collection
description: The MongoDB users collection may be subject to data corruption, tampering, or loss due to inadequate backup procedures, insufficient access controls, or system failures, compromising the integrity of stored parent account information.

title: Unintended data disclosure through metadata
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may be inadvertently disclosed through metadata leakage, log files, or incidental data exposure during system operations, even if the primary data is protected.

title: JWT and user data transmitted without adequate encryption
description: Authentication Service sends JWT tokens and user data to Parent User via external flow. If not properly encrypted during transmission, sensitive authentication credentials and personal information could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.

title: Information leakage of authentication credentials
description: JWT tokens containing authentication information and user data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission to Parent User, potentially compromising user identity and access.

title: Unauthorized access to authentication data by parent user
description: Parent User may access JWT tokens and user data without proper authorization or consent, potentially violating privacy regulations and user expectations.

title: Unauthorized interception of login credentials
description: Parent email and password transmitted from child user to authentication service may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to credential compromise.

title: Loss of authentication data during transmission
description: Authentication credentials may be lost or corrupted during transmission from child user to authentication service, potentially causing authentication failures.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child credentials
description: Parent email and password may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the login process, violating child privacy and data protection requirements.

title: Authentication service unavailability during login
description: Authentication service may become unavailable during login attempts, preventing child users from accessing their accounts and services.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Authentication process may not comply with child-specific privacy regulations and data protection requirements for handling parent email and password information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profiles during authentication
description: Child profiles transmitted from Authentication Service to Child User may be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.

title: Loss of JWT authentication tokens during transmission
description: JWT tokens containing user type information may be lost or corrupted during transmission from Authentication Service to Child User, potentially causing authentication failures or requiring re-authentication.

title: Unintended data exposure to external entities
description: Child profiles and JWT information may be exposed to unintended external entities or systems during the authentication flow, potentially violating privacy expectations.

title: Linking of child profile data with other data sources
description: Parent user may link child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with other data sources (e.g., other children, parent records, external databases) to build comprehensive profiles that reveal additional information about the child beyond what is explicitly collected.
assumptions: Parent may have access to or ability to correlate child data with other records

title: Inference of sensitive information from collected data
description: From the collected child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID), sensitive inferences could be made about the child's age, family composition, location, and other characteristics that may not be explicitly collected but can be inferred.
assumptions: Data collection includes identifiable information that can be used for inference

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile information
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls during profile creation and storage.
assumptions: Profile data is stored and processed by the system

title: Duplicate child profile creation
description: Multiple duplicate child profiles may be created for the same child, leading to data redundancy and potential privacy concerns from inconsistent or conflicting information.
assumptions: System may not have effective deduplication mechanisms

title: Unintended consequences of profile creation
description: Child profile creation may have unintended consequences such as affecting the child's future opportunities, creating permanent records, or enabling tracking across services.
assumptions: Profile data may be used beyond the intended scope

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the MongoDB collection during the store/update operation, violating privacy principles and potentially exposing sensitive personal information about children.

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may be accessed by unauthorized users or systems, leading to potential exposure of child profile information.

title: Unauthorized deletion of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be deleted without proper authorization or due to system errors, resulting in loss of important personal information.

title: Unintended use of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be used in ways not intended by the system design, such as being shared with third parties or used for purposes beyond the original scope.

title: Unencrypted transmission of user search queries
description: User's video search queries and preferences transmitted from ExternalEntity to Process without proper encryption, potentially exposing sensitive search behavior to interception.

title: Leakage of user interaction history
description: User's search history, like, and comment data could be leaked during transmission or stored without proper access controls, potentially exposing personal viewing preferences.

title: Data integrity of user interaction records
description: User's like and comment data stored in the Video Management Service could be corrupted, altered, or tampered with, affecting the accuracy of user activity records.

title: Non-compliance with data retention policies
description: User's video search, like, and comment data may not be retained or deleted according to applicable privacy regulations, potentially leading to data over-retention or premature deletion.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain identifying information about users (e.g., timestamps, locations, device identifiers, user IDs) that could be used to identify individuals even without access to the video content itself.
assumptions: Video metadata includes user-related information that could be linked to specific individuals.

title: Implicit data disclosure through metadata storage
description: Storing video metadata in a data store may result in implicit disclosure of personal data to third parties through data breaches, unauthorized access, or data sharing practices, even if the video content itself is not directly disclosed.
assumptions: Data store may be accessed by third parties or may be subject to data sharing practices.

title: Unauthorized access to stored video data
description: Stored video files and metadata in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to potential privacy violations through exposure of personal information.
assumptions: MongoDB data store may be vulnerable to unauthorized access or data breaches.

title: Unintended disclosure of child search history
description: Child search and watch history may be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leakage, or insufficient encryption during storage in MongoDB collection.

title: Explicit disclosure of child watch history
description: Child watch history may be intentionally shared with third parties (e.g., advertisers, data brokers) without proper consent or minimality principle compliance.

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Unauthorized users may access child search and watch history stored in MongoDB collection due to insufficient authentication or authorization controls.

title: Data integrity compromise of child history
description: Stored child search and watch history may be corrupted, tampered with, or altered without proper integrity controls and audit mechanisms.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storage of child search and watch history may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy regulations due to insufficient data minimization, consent management, or retention policies.

title: Unauthorized video upload access
description: Parent User (EE1) may upload videos to Video Management Service (P2) without proper authentication, allowing unauthorized users to access the upload functionality.

title: Confidentiality of uploaded video data
description: Video content uploaded by Parent User (EE1) may contain personal data that could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to Video Management Service (P2).

title: Data integrity during upload
description: Video data uploaded by Parent User (EE1) may be corrupted or tampered with during transmission to Video Management Service (P2), compromising data integrity.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Video upload process by Parent User (EE1) to Video Management Service (P2) may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding personal data handling.

title: Unauthorized access to video stream
description: Video content may be accessed by unauthorized users without proper authentication and authorization controls
assumptions: Assumes video stream lacks proper access control mechanisms

title: Lack of confidentiality during video transmission
description: Video content may be intercepted or exposed during transmission to child user without proper encryption
assumptions: Assumes video stream may not be encrypted in transit

title: Data integrity during video streaming
description: Video content may be tampered with or corrupted during transmission to child user
assumptions: Assumes video stream may not have integrity protection mechanisms

title: Intentional disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) is planned to transfer browsing data to Third-Party Advertisers (EE3). This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal browsing information is shared with external entities for advertising purposes, potentially without adequate user consent or transparency about the scope and purpose of data sharing.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information about user behavior and preferences

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, leading to potential privacy breaches of sensitive personal data.

title: Inadequate Access Controls on Data Store
description: The file system backend/uploads/ may lack sufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized users to access or modify stored government ID images.

title: Metadata Exposure of Stored Files
description: File metadata (timestamps, file names, permissions) may reveal information about when and how government ID images were stored, potentially exposing patterns or sensitive information.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure Through Storage
description: Government ID images may be inadvertently disclosed through improper storage configurations, such as insufficient encryption or lack of data retention policies.

title: JWT stored in localStorage may be intercepted by malicious scripts
description: Browser localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running in the same origin. Malicious scripts can read localStorage contents, potentially stealing JWT tokens and compromising user authentication.
assumptions: Assumes localStorage is accessible to malicious scripts in the same origin context.

title: JWT contains user identifiers enabling cross-session linking
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers that can be used to link user activity across different sessions and services, potentially enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains identifiable user information.

title: JWT storage in localStorage may exceed necessary retention period
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage may result in tokens persisting longer than necessary, increasing the window of opportunity for attackers to exploit compromised credentials.
assumptions: Assumes no automatic token rotation or expiration mechanism is in place.

title: Child-Parent Linking via Profile Data
description: The process retrieves child history data and transmits it to the parent user, creating a linkage between child data and parent identity. This enables the system to associate child records with parent accounts, potentially allowing for profile building across multiple children or enabling tracking of parent-child relationships beyond intended scope.
assumptions: The system uses parent identifiers to retrieve and transmit child data

title: Sensitive Child History Disclosure to Parent
description: Child history data may contain sensitive personal information about the child (e.g., behavioral patterns, academic records, health information) that is disclosed to the parent user. This disclosure could reveal more about the child than the parent is authorized to know, or could be used for unintended profiling purposes.
assumptions: Child history contains sensitive personal data

title: Child History Data Quality Issues
description: The child history data retrieved by the process may be incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated, leading to decisions based on flawed information. This could result in inappropriate parental decisions or misunderstandings about the child's situation.
assumptions: Child history data is subject to quality control issues
